newsitem.title: ITALY: U.N. agency apologises to China over Taiwan slip.
newsitem.headline: U.N. agency apologises to China over Taiwan slip.

text.p: The U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) apologised to Chinese Premier Li Peng on Friday after identifying him as leader of arch-rival Taiwan in an official document at the World Food Summit.

The written Journal containing the programme of speakers for Friday's sessions of the World Food Summit at FAO's Rome headquarters referred to Li as "Premier of the State Council of the Republic of China".
That is the official name of Taiwan, which Beijing does not recognise as an independent country.
Communist China's official name is "The People's Republic of China".
"We regret that this omission was made," a summit official told delegates in a special announcement.
"A new journal is now being corrected and will be distributed to you as soon as possible," the official said.
Li was scheduled to address the summit on Friday afternoon.
